items.title: Graded module and projective Grothendieck groups of the KLR and Hecke towers
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $R=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in Q_+}R_\alpha$ be a tower of finite-dimensional unital $\mathbb Z$-graded $k$-algebras with local units $e(\alpha)$ summing to the identity of $R$ in the locally finite sense, each $R_\alpha$ a direct summand and $R_0=k$. Define $$K_0^{\rm gr}(R):=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in Q_+}K_0^{\rm gr}(R_\alpha),\qquad G_0^{\rm gr}(R):=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in Q_+}G_0^{\rm gr}(R_\alpha),$$ the restricted direct sums of the blockwise Grothendieck groups of [[def-graded-grothendieck-group-shift-module-and-cartan-map]]: $K_0^{\rm gr}(R_\alpha)$ of finitely generated graded left $R_\alpha$-projectives modulo split exact sequences and $G_0^{\rm gr}(R_\alpha)$ of finite-dimensional graded left $R_\alpha$-modules modulo short exact sequences. Both are modules over $A:=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ by $q[M]:=[M\{1\}]$, and inside each finite-dimensional block the shift-orbit bases of [[thm-graded-projective-and-simple-classes-have-shift-orbit-bases]] hold. The Cartan homomorphism $c:K_0^{\rm gr}(R)\to G_0^{\rm gr}(R)$, $[P]\mapsto[P]$, is $A$-linear. The forgetful maps $\zeta$ to the ungraded groups $K_0(R)$, $G_0(R)$ are additive and satisfy $\zeta(qm)=m$. The groups $K_0^{\rm gr}$ and $G_0^{\rm gr}$ are DIFFERENT objects and are never identified.

**The two towers used below.** (i) For the standard homogeneous cyclotomic quotient of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]] at the level-one weight $\Lambda_0$ of [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]], put $R^\Lambda_\alpha=R^\Lambda(\alpha)$; every block is finite dimensional and has the homogeneous symmetrizing functional of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-algebras-are-finite-dimensional-graded-symmetric]], with grading shifts as in [[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]. (ii) For the cyclotomic Hecke tower $H^{\Lambda}:=\bigoplus_\alpha H^\Lambda_\alpha$ of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]] with the block decomposition of [[def-residue-sequence-idempotents-and-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks]], fix an admissible local normalising series and transport the homogeneous KLR decomposition through the blockwise isomorphism of [[thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism]], as in [[cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading]]; the induced transport identifies $K_0^{\rm gr}(H^{\Lambda})\cong K_0^{\rm gr}(R^\Lambda)$ as $A$-modules and similarly for $G_0^{\rm gr}$, compatibly with $\zeta$ and with the Cartan homomorphisms. Every class has finite root support, so the direct sums are restricted.

No choice principle is used in this definition.
items.strategy: Instantiate [[def-graded-grothendieck-group-shift-module-and-cartan-map]] blockwise: finiteness of each block is [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-algebras-are-finite-dimensional-graded-symmetric]], so the simple and projective shift-orbit bases of [[thm-graded-projective-and-simple-classes-have-shift-orbit-bases]] apply without a positivity assumption; a finite-support combination of block classes is again finite-support because $Q_+$-degree is additive, which makes the restricted direct sums $A$-modules and makes $c$ and $\zeta$ well defined. The Hecke-side identification is transport of structure along the graded algebra isomorphism: [[thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism]] matches each residue-content block with its KLR block, and [[cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading]] supplies the grading; the induced functor on graded modules is exact and preserves projectives (proved on its own as the transport lemma below), so it induces the stated isomorphisms of Grothendieck groups. The separate-group warning is the point of the definition.

items.title: The graded Cartan pairing between projective and module classes
items.statement:
In the situation and notation of [[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]], for each root degree $\alpha$, finite-dimensional graded left $R^\Lambda_\alpha$-modules $M$ and finitely generated graded projective $P$ put $$h_\alpha(P,M):=\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}_{R^\Lambda_\alpha}(P,M)=\sum_{d\in\mathbb Z}q^d\dim_k\operatorname{Hom}_{R^\Lambda_\alpha,d}(P,M)\in A .$$ By [[thm-projective-hom-pairing-is-additive-and-graded-sesquilinear]] (whose finite-dimensional hypotheses hold blockwise) this descends to an $A$-sesquilinear pairing $$h:K_0^{\rm gr}(R^\Lambda)\times G_0^{\rm gr}(R^\Lambda)\longrightarrow A,$$ with the twist $q\mapsto q^{-1}$: $h(q^r[P],q^s[M])=q^{s-r}h([P],[M])$. In particular $h^0(P,S):=\dim_k\operatorname{Hom}^0(P,S)$ is the degree-zero part. The pairing on the Hecke side is the transported pairing of [[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]]. Also fix the two dualities used below: the descended anti-involution $\psi$ of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals]] with its finite-module duality $D_\psi$ and finite-projective duality $\#$, both shift-reversing and involutive on their domains; and the convention that a simple module or projective cover is called *normalized* when it is fixed (not merely fixed up to shift) by the relevant duality and, for a cover, when $\operatorname{Hom}^0(P,S)=k$.

No perfectness, nondegeneracy or $A$-self-duality is asserted in this definition; those are supplied by [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-module-g-zero-is-the-dual-integral-highest-weight-module]] and its transported form on the Hecke side.
items.strategy: Specialize [[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]] and [[thm-projective-hom-pairing-is-additive-and-graded-sesquilinear]] to each finite-dimensional block $R^\Lambda_\alpha$; the finite support of the graded Hom spaces and the bilinearity/sesquilinearity reindexing are those of the cited theorem. Blockwise summability is the restricted sum of the previous definition. The duality clauses copy [[def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals]]; the claim that each simple or projective orbit has a unique normalized representative up to isomorphism is that definition's quotient-cover lemma, not a new assertion here. No choice.

items.title: The nondegenerate root-of-unity level-one Hecke regime
items.statement:
**Parameters.** Let $F$ be a field and $\xi\in F^\times$ with finite quantum characteristic $e=e(F,\xi)\in\{2,3,\dots\}$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]). We work in the NONDEGENERATE branch $\xi\ne1$; then $\xi$ is a primitive $e$-th root of unity in $F$, and all statements on this page live in one of the two sub-branches: (C0) $\operatorname{char}F=0$, or (CP) $\operatorname{char}F=p>0$ with $p\nmid e$. The Hecke parameter is written $\xi$ here; it is the letter $q$ of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]].

**Hecke side.** Fix the level-one fundamental weight $\Lambda_0$ of the cyclic affine type-$A$ datum with all $d_i=1$ and charge $0$ ([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). With the conventions of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]], $H^\Lambda_d=H_{F,\xi}(S_d)$ is the finite type-$A$ Hecke algebra $T_r^2=(\xi-1)T_r+\xi$ ([[prop-cyclotomic-hecke-algebras-of-level-one-are-finite-hecke-algebras]]), and $H^\Lambda_\alpha=e_\alpha H^\Lambda_d$ are its residue-content blocks ([[def-residue-sequence-idempotents-and-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks]]).

**KLR side.** Use the type-$A$ specialization $Q^A$ of [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]] with the same $e$ and the STANDARD homogeneous first-strand cyclotomic quotient $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]]: the cyclotomic relation is $y_1^{\delta_{i_1,0}}e(i)=0$, induction appends on the right, and the grading is $\deg e(i)=0$, $\deg y_r=2$, $\deg\psi_re(i)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ ([[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]). The transported grading on $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ uses a FIXED admissible local normalising series ([[cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading]]); a different series gives a graded-isomorphic transported algebra via $\rho'\rho^{-1}$, and the graded multiplicities studied below do not depend on the choice.

**Grading and Fock variables.** All grading shifts and all global-basis polynomials are in the variable $q$, $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. Thus $\xi\in F^\times$ (the Hecke parameter, equal to the source's $\xi$) and $q$ (the grading variable, equal to the source's quantum variable) are INDEPENDENT data; the design's phrase "Ariki's normalization $\xi=q^2$" is retained only as the source dictionary of [Ariki 1996], whose Hecke parameters are powers of a square $q_{\rm src}^2$, and no numerical relation or specialization between $\xi$ and $q$ is imposed.

**Fock side.** Use the level-one symmetric model $\mathcal F_{\rm sym}$ of [[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]]: charge $0$, node residues $c-r$, standard vectors $M_\mu$ for ALL partitions $\mu$, basic/restricted labels the $e$-restricted partitions $RP_\alpha=\{\lambda:\lambda_a-\lambda_{a+1}<e,\ \operatorname{cont}(\lambda)=\alpha\}$, empty component $B(\Lambda_0)$. For $\lambda\in RP$ let $\lambda'$ be the conjugate, which is $e$-regular and labels the Hecke simple module in the Dipper-James convention of [[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]; at $e=p$ prime and $\xi=1$ this is the published [[prop-p-regular-and-p-restricted-simple-labels-are-related-by-conjugate-sign-duality]].

No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Direct convention check. At level one $(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)=\delta_{i,0}$, so the cyclotomic polynomial of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]] is $\prod_i(X_1-\xi^i)^{(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)}=X_1-1$ and the KLR cyclotomic relation is $y_1^{\delta_{i_1,0}}e(i)=0$; the finite-characteristic hypothesis $e\in\{2,3,\dots\}$ makes $\xi\ne1$ a primitive $e$-th root, and in sub-branch (CP) the hypothesis $p\nmid e$ is exactly what makes a primitive $e$-th root exist in $F$. The type-$A$ datum and the grading are batch-24 clauses; the transport statement is the graded block isomorphism of [[thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism]] with [[cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading]]. The Fock-side residues, the restricted labels and the empty component are batch-9/batch-23 clauses. The dictionary to the $e$-regular Dipper-James labels is the recorded convention of [[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]] together with the published conjugate-sign proposition; for the Hecke side with general finite $e$ no prime-field statement is inferred, since that proposition is stated for $k[S_n]$ in characteristic $p$. The parameter dictionary is the naming clause of [BK 2009 §1 and §4.2] and [Ariki 1996 §1]; it makes no substitution. No choice is used.

items.title: A graded algebra isomorphism transports the graded module category, its Grothendieck groups and its dualities
items.statement:
Let $\rho:R\to H$ be an isomorphism of finite-dimensional unital $\mathbb Z$-graded $k$-algebras. Restriction of scalars along $\rho$ is an equivalence of graded left module categories which is exact, sends finite-dimensional modules to finite-dimensional modules, sends a shift $M\{r\}$ to $M\{r\}$, sends finitely generated graded projectives to finitely generated graded projectives, preserves composition multiplicities of graded simples (with shifts), and identifies the graded Hom pairings $\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}$ of [[def-graded-cartan-pairing-between-projectives-and-modules]]. It therefore induces $A$-module isomorphisms $K_0^{\rm gr}(R)\to K_0^{\rm gr}(H)$ and $G_0^{\rm gr}(R)\to G_0^{\rm gr}(H)$ intertwining the Cartan homomorphisms and the forgetful maps $\zeta$.

If moreover $\rho$ intertwines fixed anti-automorphisms $\ast_R$ and $\ast_H$ (i.e. $\rho(x^{\ast_R})=\rho(x)^{\ast_H}$), then the transported functor intertwines the two diagram dualities $D_\psi$ and the two projective Hom-dualities $\#$ of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals]], and hence preserves normalized self-dual simples and normalized self-dual indecomposable projectives.

**Application.** For each nonzero content sector choose the actual graded block isomorphism rho_alpha. DEFINE the Hecke duality by star_H=rho_alpha star_R rho_alpha^{-1}. This is a grading-preserving anti-involution, fixing the NAMED images of e(i),y_r,psi_r, and rho_alpha intertwines it by definition. Thus the preceding duality conclusion applies blockwise. This does not identify star_H with the raw cellular anti-involution that fixes affine Hecke generators, and does not infer that a product is fixed merely because its factors are fixed.
items.strategy: An algebra isomorphism gives inverse exact restriction-of-scalars functors, identity on the underlying graded vector spaces. It preserves shifts, finite dimension and finite free modules; retracts of finite free modules remain projective. Graded Hom spaces agree by the identity on maps, hence composition multiplicities, K0/G0, Cartan and forgetful maps agree. For finite duals, (a f)(m)=f(star_R(a)m) matches the transported formula because rho star_R=star_H rho; the identical substitution in Hom_R(P,R) identifies projective Hom duals. In the application define star_H by conjugation, which proves anti-multiplicativity and involutivity immediately; generator fixation is fixation of the rho-images. Products are reversed by star_H, so no claim about the raw affine-Hecke cellular star is used. This exact computation proves the transported self-dual and degree-zero head normalization clauses. No choice.

items.title: The QG-8 categorification transports across the blockwise Hecke-KLR bridge
items.strategy: Apply [[lem-graded-algebra-isomorphism-transports-the-graded-module-category]] to $\rho_\alpha$: the functor is exact, preserves finite modules, projectives, shifts and Hom pairings, so it induces the two $A$-module isomorphisms and preserves the displayed intertwiners and pairings; the divided-power intertwiners transport because the Hecke-side $E_i,F_i$ are defined to be the transported KLR functors ([[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]] records this convention). The perfectness statement is clause (2)+(3) of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-module-g-zero-is-the-dual-integral-highest-weight-module]] transported, not a new computation. For clause (4), check the hypotheses: the type-$A$ specialization of [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]] has $d_i=1$, the quiver is the finite loopless cycle (double edge only at $e=2$), and $Q^A$ is $(-1)^{h}(u-v)^{h+h}$ with $h=1$ on each edge, so it lies in the stated geometric parameter regime; transport the lower/upper global-basis identifications and the cover/simple crystal correspondence of [[thm-simple-and-indecomposable-projective-crystals-agree-with-b-lambda]]. The label statement is the transported crystal label. No new choice: AC enters only through the global-basis theorems' inherited hypotheses, which are declared.

items.title: The graded Specht module by homogeneous standard tableaux
items.statement:
Work in the regime of [[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]]. Fix a partition $\mu$, put $d=|\mu|$, $\alpha=\operatorname{cont}(\mu)$, and let $K(\mu)$ be the $F$-span of the Murphy elements $m_{S,T}$ of [[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]] with $S,T$ standard tableaux of a multipartition strictly dominating $\mu$; by [[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]] $K(\mu)$ is a two-sided ideal of $H^\Lambda_d$ and $z_\mu:=m_{t^\mu t^\mu}+K(\mu)$ is defined. Define the (level-one) **cell/Specht module** $$S(\mu):=H^\Lambda_d\,z_\mu\subseteq H^\Lambda_d/K(\mu),$$ a LEFT $H^\Lambda_d$-module lying in the block $H^\Lambda_\alpha$.

For every standard $\mu$-tableau $T$ fix a reduced decomposition $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$ of the associated permutation and put $z_T:=T_{w_T}z_\mu$, $v_T:=\psi_{w_T}z_\mu$ in the Khovanov-Lauda presentation of [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]]. For a removable $i$-node $A$ of a partition $\lambda$ define $d_A(\lambda):=\#\{\text{addable }i\text{-nodes strictly below }A\}-\#\{\text{removable }i\text{-nodes strictly below }A\}$ (equivalently in the level-one symmetric residue convention of the regime) and define the **degree** of a standard tableau inductively by $\deg(\varnothing):=0$ and, for $d>0$, $\deg(T):=\deg(T_{\le d-1})+d_A(\mu)$ where $A$ is the node of $T$ containing $d$.

The definition asserts, and proves below in [[thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis]], that $\{v_T:T\in\operatorname{Std}(\mu)\}$ is a homogeneous $F$-basis of $S(\mu)$ making it a graded $R^\Lambda_\alpha$-module whose $q$-character is $\operatorname{ch}_qS(\mu)=\sum_T q^{\deg T}i_T$; forgetting the grading recovers the ungraded cell module. **Convention.** $S(\mu)$ is the cell module of the Dipper-James-Mathas cellular structure; it is the DUAL of the module called Specht module in [[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]. Consequently the restricted (respectively $e$-regular) labels belong to $S(\mu)$ with $\mu$ restricted (respectively conjugate $e$-regular) in the convention of [[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]] and [[prop-p-regular-and-p-restricted-simple-labels-are-related-by-conjugate-sign-duality]]; no statement about $S(\mu)$ is silently transferred to the other convention. The labelling of simples by $e$-restricted or $e$-regular partitions is NOT asserted here; it is determined by the head-classification theorem later on this page.

No choice is used in the definition.
items.strategy: This is a definition with its construction; the asserted basis, homogeneity and module structure are discharged by [[thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis]], and the ideal/cellular facts by [[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]]. The degree recursion is the source's (4.33); the vectors $v_T$ depend a priori on the chosen reduced decompositions, and the theorem proves the resulting grading is well defined. The dictionary to [[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]] is recorded as a convention, exactly as the source records that its $S(\mu)$ is the dual of the older Specht module [BKW §4.1]. No choice. Use the LEFT-handed Murphy basis: if the supplied cellular datum is right-handed, apply its anti-involution to every basis identity. Then H z_mu is a left cyclic cell module, z_T=T_w z_mu and v_T=psi_w z_mu are left actions, consistent with the left KLR modules and right-append corner functors used throughout. No identification of a right module with a left module without this conversion is made.

items.title: The domination order on tableaux, Garnir tableaux and bricks
items.statement:
Retain English Young diagrams and row-reading initial standard tableau t^mu. For a mu-tableau T let w_T t^mu=T. The STRONG Bruhat order on tableaux is S<=_B T iff w_S<=w_T in the permutation Bruhat order. For row-strict S,T this is equivalent to the prefix shape of S DOMINATING the prefix shape of T for every prefix; it is distinct from weak Bruhat order and must not reverse this dominance direction. The transposition criterion is S=(a1 b1)...(am bm)T with an<bn and bn occupying an earlier row-reading node than an at each backward step.

For entries r,s in one component define r right-arrow_T s when they lie in the SAME row and s is strictly to the right; r down-arrow_T s when they lie in the SAME column and s is strictly below; and r northeast_T s when s is strictly ABOVE and strictly RIGHT of r. Southwest is the reverse northeast relation. A weak Bruhat graph edge T --r--> S requires both tableaux standard, S=s_r T, and r occupying an earlier row-reading node than r+1. Equivalently r+1 northeast_T r, or r is in an earlier component than r+1. In particular a same-column or same-row swap is NOT a standard edge. Terminal paths are directed paths ending at T.

The Garnir belt at (a,b,n) consists of the row-a tail from b and the row-(a+1) prefix through b. Its Garnir tableau is the maximal standard tableau in the strong Bruhat order agreeing with t^mu outside that belt. A horizontal brick is a string of consecutive entries along SAME-row right arrows. The following source facts are retained with these exact conventions: the transposition/prefix-shape criterion; the row-strictness of a vertical swap and its exceptional-prefix comparison; agreement outside the Garnir belt for lower tableaux; and the four terminal alternatives for a horizontal or vertical consecutive pair. For a horizontal pair the last alternative is T=t^mu; for a vertical pair it is the corresponding Garnir tableau. These finite combinatorial facts are proved in the strategy. No choice.
items.strategy: Permutation Bruhat order is characterized by successive inversions of transpositions with the larger entry in an earlier position; placing these entries in row-reading positions gives the transposition criterion. For row-strict tableaux count the entries <=a in each row: the Bruhat rank inequalities are exactly dominance of their prefix row-count shapes, with S dominating T when w_S<=w_T. This proves the prefix criterion and its direction (the row-reading initial tableau is Bruhat-minimal and has dominant prefixes). A consecutive swap is standard exactly for strict northeast/southwest positions or different components; same-row and same-column pairs violate row/column increase. Combine this with earlier row-reading position to obtain the directed edge criterion. For a vertical consecutive swap, only prefix a=r changes; row-strictness is immediate and the exceptional-prefix comparison follows by moving its box between those two rows. Sorting each row converts the same transposition criterion to the row-strict Bruhat comparison. A tableau below a Garnir tableau can change only positions within its belt: outside row prefixes coincide, so the same rank inequalities force those entries to remain fixed. For a consecutive horizontal pair test, in order, existence of a distant terminal interchange preserving the pair, then the two adjacent terminal paths (r,r+1) and (r,r-1). If none exists, the positions r-1,...,1 and r+2,...,d are forced into row-reading order, hence T=t^mu. The identical test for a vertical pair forces exactly the maximal belt filling if none of the first three alternatives holds. This supplies the local terminal reductions used by the two-part graded-Specht induction; bricks are horizontal, not vertical chains. Actual BKW §§3.2–3.4 source proof and positional conditions checked, no finite sample computation substitutes for the general criterion. No choice.

items.title: Degree and codegree of standard tableaux
items.strategy: Separate below and above counts. Removing the removable i-node A changes the total addable-minus-removable count by the Cartan column, and A becomes an addable node in mu^A. Splitting all remaining i-nodes into strictly above and strictly below A gives d_A(mu)+d^A(mu^A)=d_i(mu)+1. Induction from the empty diagram and the same local boundary changes gives d_i(mu)=(Lambda0-alpha,alpha_i). Expanding defect(alpha)-defect(alpha-alpha_i) using (alpha_i,alpha_i)=2 gives d_i(mu)+1. Induct on the number of nodes in the degree/codegree recursion to obtain their sum equal to defect. For a horizontal terminal brick, codegree counts strictly ABOVE it: the first row has no such nodes; an e-brick contains every residue once and above boundary addable/removable contributions cancel. This proves both brick clauses. Check e2 shape(2): below degree1, above codegree0, defect1; shape(1,1): degree0, above codegree1, defect1. These checks illustrate, not replace, the boundary count proof. No choice.

items.title: Shifted degrees and Garnir exchanges for standard tableaux
items.statement:
In the situation of [[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]]:

1. If $T\xrightarrow{\,r\,}S$ (i.e. $r\to_T r+1$ and $S=s_rT$), then $\deg(S)-\deg(T)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$, where $i_T=(i_1,\dots,i_d)$ and $a$ is the Cartan matrix of the regime.
2. More generally, if $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$ is a reduced decomposition, then $\deg(T)-\deg(t^\mu)=\deg\bigl(\psi_{r_1}\cdots\psi_{r_m}e(i_{t^\mu})\bigr)$ in the grading of [[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]].
3. If $T$ is the $(a,b)$-Garnir tableau with entry $r$ in the node $(a,b)$, and $S$ is a standard $\mu$-tableau with $S\lhd T$ and $i_S=i_{s_rT}$, then $\deg(S)-\deg(T)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ as well.

No choice is used.
items.strategy: 1 is [BKW, Proposition 3.13]: reduce to $r=d-1$ and compare the two expressions for $\deg(T)$ and $\deg(S)$; the difference is $d_B(\mu^A)-d_B(\mu)$ for the nodes $A$ (containing $d$) and $B$ (containing $d-1$), and the four residue cases (equal residues, adjacent single edge, the $e=2$ double edge, and non-adjacent) give exactly $-2,1,2,0=-a_{i_{d-1}i_d}$. 2 is [BKW, Corollary 3.14], obtained from 1 by multiplying the adjacent transpositions of the reduced word and adding the degrees $\deg(\psi_re(i_T))$. 3 is [BKW, Proposition 3.16]: using the tableau-order Lemma 3.9 reduce to a two-row Garnir belt; the exchange condition $i_S=i_{s_rT}$ splits the belt into bricks of size divisible by $e$ plus at most one exceptional brick per row; Lemma 3.15 computes $\operatorname{codeg}(S)$ and $\operatorname{codeg}(T)$ by the congruence classes of $b$ modulo $e$, and the difference is $-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ in each case. All steps are finite residue and brick computations; no choice. For the strict Garnir case retain the maximal standard belt tableau and strict Bruhat lower condition. Reduce to a two-row belt ending at its final node by the agreement-outside-belt lemma. Remove complete horizontal e-bricks using the ABOVE codegree lemma. The lower tableau has residual codegree -1 if b is nonzero modulo e and 0 otherwise. The Garnir tableau has codegree0/1 for e>2, and1/2 for e=2, respectively. Their difference gives degree1/2 in the single/double-edge cases. Equal-color degree in a standard exchange remains -2, from the Cartan diagonal; it is not assigned +2.

items.title: The graded Specht module has a homogeneous tableau basis
items.statement:
Keep the notation of [[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]]; the vectors $v_T=\psi_{w_T}z_\mu$ may a priori depend on the chosen reduced decompositions $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$. Then:

1. For every $\mu$-tableau $T$ one has $v_T=\sum_{S\unlhd T}a_Sz_S$ with $a_T\ne0$ when $T$ is standard; hence the standard vectors form a basis of $S(\mu)$ triangular with respect to the standard basis $\{z_T\}$ of [[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]].
2. If $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}=s_{t_1}\cdots s_{t_m}$ are two reduced decompositions of the same $w_T$, then $\psi_{r_1}\cdots\psi_{r_m}z_\mu-\psi_{t_1}\cdots\psi_{t_m}z_\mu=\sum_{S\unlhd T,\ i_S=i_T,\ \deg S=\deg T}a_Sv_S$; in particular the grading on $S(\mu)$ defined by $\deg(v_T):=\deg(T)$ is independent of the choices.
3. For every $r$ the vectors $e(i)v_T$, $y_rv_T$ and $\psi_rv_T$ are homogeneous, with $$e(i)v_T=\delta_{i,i_T}v_T,\qquad \deg(y_rv_T)=\deg(y_r)+\deg(T),\qquad \deg(\psi_rv_T)=\deg(\psi_re(i_T))+\deg(T).$$ Hence $S(\mu)$ is a graded $R^\Lambda_\alpha$-module with homogeneous basis $\{v_T\}$ and $q$-character $\operatorname{ch}_qS(\mu)=\sum_{T\in\operatorname{Std}(\mu)}q^{\deg T}i_T$; forgetting the grading recovers the ungraded cell module of [[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]].

No choice beyond the finite selections of reduced decompositions is used; the resulting graded isomorphism class is independent of them by (2).
items.strategy: Follow [BKW, §4.2-4.3]: (1) expand $\psi_{r_1}\cdots\psi_{r_m}z_\mu$ in the standard basis using the quadratic relation, the dot-sliding relations and Lemma 4.1 ($y_rz_\mu=0$, $X_rz_\mu=\xi^{i_r}z_\mu$), and use Proposition 4.3 (triangularity of the $z$-basis) to identify the leading coefficient, which is nonzero exactly for standard $T$. (2) By Matsumoto's theorem it suffices to compare two words differing by one braid relation; the quadratic/braid relations express the difference as a combination of shorter words with the stated weight and degree, and induction on length plus (1) gives the claim. (3) Compute $y_rv_T$ and $\psi_rv_T$ by moving the generators through the reduced word using the mixed relations; every occurring vector has weight $i_T$ or $i_{s_rT}$ and the degrees follow from [[prop-shifted-degrees-and-garnir-exchanges-for-standard-tableaux]] (1) and the definition of $\deg(T)$; the codegree identities of [[lem-degree-and-codegree-of-standard-tableaux]] supply the bookkeeping in the terminal/Garnir cases. The $q$-character formula is then immediate from the homogeneous basis, and forgetting the grading gives the ungraded cell module by construction. This is [BKW, Theorem 4.10] restated; the independence statement is its part (i). No choice.

items.title: Graded Specht restriction has the removable-node filtration
items.statement:
Keep the notation of [[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]], let $\mu$ be a partition of $d$, $\alpha=\operatorname{cont}(\mu)$, and let $i\in I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$. Let $A_1,\dots,A_c$ be the removable $i$-nodes of $\mu$ ordered from bottom to top, and let $\mu^{A_m}=\mu\setminus A_m$. Write $E_i:=E_i^{\rm basic}$ for the restriction functor $N\mapsto e(\alpha-\alpha_i,\alpha_i)N$ of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]] (equivalently the $i$-part of the tower restriction of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]]). Then $E_iS(\mu)$ has a filtration $$0=V_0\subset V_1\subset\cdots\subset V_c=E_iS(\mu)$$ of graded $R^\Lambda_{\alpha-\alpha_i}$-modules with $V_m/V_{m-1}\cong S(\mu^{A_m})\{d_{A_m}(\mu)\}$ for $1\le m\le c$.

Equivalently, the restriction of $S(\mu)$ to the previous rank has the removable-node filtration of [BKW, Theorem 4.11] over ALL removable nodes, and $E_i$ selects the removable-$i$-node part. No choice is used.
items.strategy: By [[thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis]] the module $S(\mu)$ has the homogeneous tableau basis $\{v_T\}$ with $v_T\in e(i_T)S(\mu)$, so the idempotent projection $e(\alpha-\alpha_i,\alpha_i)S(\mu)$ is spanned by those $v_T$ whose last letter is $i$, i.e. whose maximal entry $d$ occupies a removable $i$-node. Set $V_m:=\operatorname{span}\{v_T:\ d\text{ lies in }A_1\cup\cdots\cup A_m\}$; each $V_m$ is a graded $R^\Lambda_{\alpha-\alpha_i}$-submodule because the generators $y_r,\psi_r$ of the previous rank act by the degree-preserving formulas of [[thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis]] (3). The ungraded quotient identification $V_m/V_{m-1}\cong S(\mu^{A_m})$ is [AM, Proposition 1.9] as recalled in [BKW, Theorem 4.11]: deleting the maximal entry from a standard tableau with $d$ in $A_m$ gives a standard $\mu^{A_m}$-tableau, and the map $v_T+V_{m-1}\mapsto v_{T_{\le d-1}}$ is an isomorphism of $H^\Lambda_{d-1}$-modules; the grading shift is computed from the degree recursion $\deg(T)=\deg(T_{\le d-1})+d_{A_m}(\mu)$, which is exactly the shift $d_{A_m}(\mu)$. The passage from the whole restriction to $E_i$ is the idempotent decomposition $\operatorname{Res}=\bigoplus_iE_i$ of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]] and the definition of $E_i$; order the $i$-nodes bottom to top as in the source. This is [BKW, Theorem 4.11] and [BK 2009, Proposition 5.5]; the independent treatment of the (dual) induced filtration is [Hu-Mathas, Main Theorem]. No choice.

items.title: Graded Specht classes realize the standard Fock vectors
items.statement: In the regime of [[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], let $\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}:G_0^{\rm gr}(H^{\Lambda})\to V_A(\Lambda_0)^\vee$ be the transported identification of [[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]], and let $S_\mu:=\pi(M_\mu)$ be the standard monomial image of the standard Fock vector $M_\mu$ of [[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]] under the projection to the basic module. Then for every partition $\mu$ with content $\alpha$, $$\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}\bigl([S(\mu)]\bigr)=S_\mu .$$ In other words, the class of the graded Specht module of [[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]] is the standard Fock vector in the fixed level-one convention. This holds in both branches (C0) and (CP). No choice beyond the inherited suppliers is used.
items.strategy: Induct on $\operatorname{ht}(\alpha)$ following [BK 2009, Theorem 5.6]. For $\alpha=0$, $S(\emptyset)=F$ is the vacuum and $S_\emptyset=v_{\Lambda_0}$, and both sides are the class of the trivial module. For the induction step it suffices, since $V(\Lambda_0)$ is irreducible as a $\mathbb Q(q)$-module with highest weight $\Lambda_0$ and $\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}([S(\mu)])-S_\mu$ lies in the image, to show that every $E_i$ kills the difference. The transport intertwines the Hecke-side $E_i$ with the KLR $E_i$ ([[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]] (3)); by [[thm-graded-specht-restriction-has-the-removable-node-filtration]] and the definition of the filtered quotients, $E_i$ acts on $[S(\mu)]$ by $\sum_A q^{d_A(\mu)}[S(\mu^A)]$, where $A$ runs over the removable $i$-nodes, which is exactly the Fock-space recursion $E_iS_\mu=\sum_Aq^{d_A(\mu)}S_{\mu^A}$ of [[lem-semi-infinite-wedges-are-indexed-by-partitions-and-give-node-action-formulas]] and [[thm-the-fock-space-node-formulas-satisfy-the-quantum-affine-relations]]. The induction hypothesis applies to each $S(\mu^A)$, so $E_i$ annihilates the difference; irreducibility/uniqueness of the integrable highest-weight module ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]) then forces it to vanish. This is [BK 2009, Theorem 5.6] transported through the library's identifications; the argument is field-independent in the stated regime. No new choice.

items.statement: In the regime of [[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], for every residue content $\alpha$ the classes $\{[S(\lambda)]:\lambda\in RP_\alpha\}$ of the graded Specht modules with restricted shapes form an $A$-basis of $G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$, and in fact the standard vectors with all shapes of content $\alpha$ form an $A$-basis of the ambient standard lattice; the two statements are matched by [[thm-graded-specht-classes-realize-standard-fock-vectors]]. items.strategy: By [[thm-graded-specht-classes-realize-standard-fock-vectors]] the transported map $\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}$ sends $[S(\mu)]$ to $S_\mu$, and by [[thm-the-basic-representation-global-basis-is-unitriangular-in-the-partition-basis]] and [[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]] the restricted standard monomials $S_\lambda$ ($\lambda\in RP_\alpha$) form an $A$-basis of the basic lattice $V_A(\Lambda_0)$ while the full family $\{S_\mu\}$ spans the costandard lattice; since $\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}$ is an isomorphism onto the (restricted) dual and the classes $[S(\mu)]$ lie in $G_0^{\rm gr}$, the restricted classes form an $A$-basis of the free $A$-module $G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$. items.title: Standard Fock vectors expand in the upper global basis
items.statement:
In the level-one symmetric model of [[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]], let $G(\lambda)$ be the lower global basis vectors of the basic module $V_A(\Lambda_0)$ and $G^*(\lambda)$ the upper global basis vectors, normalized so that the restricted graded pairing of [[thm-upper-and-lower-global-bases-are-dual-and-crystal-compatible]] satisfies $\langle G(\lambda),G^*(
u)angle=\delta_{\lambda,
u}$ for $\lambda,
u\in RP$, and let $d_{\lambda,\mu}(q)$ be the transition polynomials of [[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]], defined by $G(\lambda)=\sum_{\mu}d_{\lambda,\mu}(q)M_\mu$. Then for every partition $\mu$: $$S_\mu=\pi(M_\mu)=\sum_{\lambda\in RP}d_{\lambda,\mu}(q)\,G^*(\lambda),$$ the sum being finite; in particular the standard monomials expand in the upper global basis with the transposed transition matrix.

Choice is inherited only through the cited global-basis suppliers.
items.strategy: Evaluate the restricted graded pairing of [[thm-upper-and-lower-global-bases-are-dual-and-crystal-compatible]] on the standard vector: by definition $\langle G(\lambda),M_\mu\rangle=d_{\lambda,\mu}(q)$ (coefficient of $M_\mu$ in $G(\lambda)$), and the ambient polarization is the $A$-bilinear form orthonormal on the standard vectors ([[thm-the-basic-representation-global-basis-is-unitriangular-in-the-partition-basis]] records that the lower global vectors are unitriangular in the standard basis and that the field form is standard-orthonormal). Since $\{G^*(\lambda)\}$ is the form-dual basis of the restricted lower span and the projection $\pi$ is compatible with the pairing ([[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]], [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]]), expanding the functional $\langle-,M_\mu\rangle$ in the dual basis gives the displayed identity. Equivalently, transpose the defining unitriangular system; no A-unit determinant or lower self-duality is used. This is [BK 2009, (3.36)] in the library's model. No new choice.

items.title: Graded decomposition numbers equal canonical-basis coefficients in characteristic zero
items.statement: In branch (C0) of the regime of [[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], for every partition $\mu$ with content $\alpha$ and every $\lambda\in RP_\alpha$, the graded composition multiplicity satisfies $$[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]_q=d_{\lambda,\mu}(q),$$ where $d_{\lambda,\mu}$ is the level-one global-basis transition polynomial of [[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]; equivalently $[S(\mu)]=\sum_{\lambda\in RP_\alpha}d_{\lambda,\mu}(q)[D(\lambda)]$ in $G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$, and $d_{\lambda,\mu}=0$ unless $\lambda\unlhd\mu$. Specializing $q=1$ gives Ariki's ungraded decomposition-number theorem $[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]=d_{\lambda,\mu}(1)$. Choice is inherited only through the QG-8 global-basis suppliers.
items.strategy: Apply the transported isomorphism $\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}$ to the class of $S(\mu)$: by [[thm-graded-specht-classes-realize-standard-fock-vectors]] it equals $S_\mu$, and by [[lem-standard-fock-vectors-expand-in-the-upper-global-basis]] $S_\mu=\sum_{\lambda}d_{\lambda,\mu}(q)G^*(\lambda)$ with the same coefficients as the lower expansion. By [[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]] (2) the vectors $G^*(\lambda)$ are the images of the simple classes $[D(\lambda)]$, so applying $(\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke})^{-1}$ yields $[S(\mu)]=\sum_\lambda d_{\lambda,\mu}(q)[D(\lambda)]$; the composition multiplicities are read off because the simple classes form a basis of the free $A$-module $G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$ ([[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]] (2)). The dominance vanishing is the support statement of [[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]. The $q=1$ specialization is the forgetful map of [[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]], and the ungraded statement is [BK 2009, Theorem 5.9] (Ariki). This is [BK 2009, Theorem 5.14 and Corollary 5.15], with [Kleshchev, Theorem 9.9] as the independent treatment. No new choice.

items.title: The integral form of the cyclotomic Hecke-KLR block
items.statement: Let $K$ be a characteristic-zero field in branch (C0) of [[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]] and fix, for each residue content $\alpha$, the Khovanov-Lauda generators $\{e(i)\}$, $\{y_r\}$, $\{\psi_r\}$ of the block $H^\Lambda_\alpha(K)$ of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]], i.e. the $\rho_\alpha$-images of the KLR generators ([[thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism]], [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]]), in a fixed admissible local normalising series. Define $$H^\Lambda_\alpha(\mathbb Z):=\bigl\langle e(i),\ y_r,\ \psi_r\ \bigr\rangle_{\mathbb Z}\subseteq H^\Lambda_\alpha(K)$$ to be the $\mathbb Z$-subring generated by them. It is the $\mathbb Z$-span of the same finite normal forms (in the Khovanov-Lauda generators) that span $H^\Lambda_\alpha(K)$ over $K$, hence a free $\mathbb Z$-module and a lattice; the generator degrees give it a grading, and the base-change maps $$K\otimes_{\mathbb Z}H^\Lambda_\alpha(\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow H^\Lambda_\alpha(K),\qquad F\otimes_{\mathbb Z}H^\Lambda_\alpha(\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow H^\Lambda_\alpha(F)$$ sending $1\otimes e(i)\mapsto e(i)$, $1\otimes y_r\mapsto y_r$, $1\otimes\psi_r\mapsto\psi_r$ are isomorphisms of graded algebras for every field $F$ of sub-branch (CP) with a primitive $e$-th root of unity, the second being the reduction modulo $p$. The direct sums over $\alpha$ give the integral form of the tower. No choice is used.
items.strategy: Use the exact integer type-A KLR presentation with generator images in each characteristic-zero sector. Integer PBW straightening spans its image by ordered dot monomials times crossing words and word idempotents. Dot nilpotence in the finite characteristic-zero standard cyclotomic quotient bounds every position; finitely many words give finitely many nonzero spanning monomials. Their Z-span is closed under integer straightening and is torsion-free inside the characteristic-zero algebra. First descend to Q: the map from the Q KLR presentation to the generator image becomes the actual BK isomorphism after extending to K; faithful field extension makes it an isomorphism already over Q. Thus the integer image is a full finite lattice in this Q-algebra, of rank equal to dim_K H_alpha(K), and K tensor this lattice is H_alpha(K). For EVERY content alpha at fixed rank the reduced named generators satisfy the integer relations and generate F tensor the lattice, giving a SURJECTION H_alpha(F) -> F tensor H_alpha(Z) via the actual field BK presentation. Consequently dim_F H_alpha(F) >= dim_K H_alpha(K) for every alpha, including zero sectors. Sum over all finitely many rank-d contents: both total dimensions equal ell^d d! by the late field basis theorem. All individual nonnegative differences therefore vanish, proving every surjection is an isomorphism. Rankzero gives the singleton unit lattice; the levelzero positive-rank quotient is zero. Homogeneity of generators and relations supplies the integer grading. This is the complete applicable BK2008 Theorems6.1/6.4 proof route, without inferring an individual block dimension directly from total dimension alone. No choice.

items.title: Reduction of characteristic-zero simple modules modulo p
items.strategy: Part 1 is [BK4, Theorem 6.5]: $H^\Lambda_\alpha(\mathbb Z)v_\lambda$ is a finitely generated $\mathbb Z$-submodule which spans $\widetilde D(\lambda)$ over $K$ because the latter is irreducible, hence it is a lattice; the weight statement follows because the $e(i)$ are idempotents in the $\mathbb Z$-form and $e(i)L(\lambda)$ is a lattice in $e(i)\widetilde D(\lambda)$. Part 2 is the graded refinement recorded after that theorem in [BK 2009, §5.6]: the generators act homogeneously on $L(\lambda)$, so $J(\lambda)$ is graded with the same $q$-character; independence of the lattice is Theorem 6.5's last sentence together with the fact that two lattices are commensurable, so their reductions have the same class in the Grothendieck group. Part 3 follows the proof of [BK 2009, Lemma 5.16]: it suffices to show that two modules over the two fields with the same $q$-character have the same image under the transported identification; by [[cor-graded-specht-classes-form-a-basis-of-the-module-grothendieck-group]] it suffices to check the classes of the graded Specht modules $S(\mu)$, for which [[thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis]] gives a field-independent $q$-character and [[thm-graded-specht-classes-realize-standard-fock-vectors]] identifies the image with $S_\mu$ over either field. Therefore $\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}([J(\lambda)])=\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}([\widetilde D(\lambda)])$, and the latter is $D_\lambda$ by the characteristic-zero canonical-basis theorem [[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]] (2). No new choice.

items.title: The graded adjustment polynomials in positive characteristic
items.statement:
In branch (CP) of the regime of [[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], with the reduced modules $J(
u)$ of [[lem-reduction-of-characteristic-zero-simple-modules-modulo-p]] and the normalized simples $D(\lambda)$ with crystal label $\lambda\in RP_\alpha$ of [[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]] (4) (in branch (C0) these are the heads of the graded Specht modules by [[thm-graded-specht-heads-classify-the-graded-simple-modules]] (3)), define the **graded adjustment polynomials** $a_{\lambda,
u}(q)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ for $\lambda,
u\in RP_\alpha$ by $$[J(
u)]=\sum_{\lambda\in RP_\alpha}a_{\lambda,
u}(q)[D(\lambda)]\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad a_{\lambda,
u}(q)=[J(
u):D(\lambda)]_q .$$ Then the matrix $(a_{\lambda,
u})$ is the graded adjustment matrix; its entries are bar-invariant, have nonnegative integer coefficients, satisfy $a_{
u,
u}(q)=1$ and vanish unless $\lambda\unlhd
u$ (dominance); equivalently $a_{\lambda,
u}$ is the coefficient of $[D(\lambda)]$ in $(\Psi_{m can}^{m Hecke})^{-1}(D_
u)$.

**Source comparison (recorded, not used).** For level one and $\xi=1$ the source states that this adjustment matrix specializes at $q=1$ to the adjustment matrix of James; that degenerate comparison lies outside the nondegenerate branch of this page and is deferred (see the batch coverage record). No choice is used in the definition.
items.strategy:
The defining expansion exists and is unique because the simple classes form a basis of $G_0^{m gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha(F))$ ([[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]] (2)); finiteness follows from finite dimensionality of $J(
u)$. Bar-invariance: the $D(\lambda)$ are $\circledast$-self-dual normalized simples ([[thm-graded-specht-heads-classify-the-graded-simple-modules]]) and $[J(
u)]$ is bar-invariant because $\Psi_{m can}^{m Hecke}([J(
u)])=D_
u$ with $D_
u$ bar-invariant ([[lem-reduction-of-characteristic-zero-simple-modules-modulo-p]] (3)); hence the coordinates $a_{\lambda,
u}$ are bar-invariant. Nonnegativity is immediate from the module interpretation $a_{\lambda,
u}=[J(
u):D(\lambda)]_q$. The diagonal and support: expand $D_
u$ in the standard Fock basis using the inverse of the dominance-unitriangular transition matrix $d$ ([[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]), apply $(\Psi_{m can}^{m Hecke})^{-1}$ and [[thm-graded-specht-classes-realize-standard-fock-vectors]], and use the dominance unitriangularity of the graded Specht-head decomposition matrix of [[thm-graded-specht-heads-classify-the-graded-simple-modules]] (2) (the graded form of [[cor-cellular-decomposition-matrices-are-dominance-unitriangular]]); multiplying the two dominance-triangular matrices gives $a_{
u,
u}=1$ and support $\lambda\unlhd
u$. This is the definition and first part of [BK 2009, Theorem 5.17] in the library's normalization; the ungraded specialization of the source's [cor-type-a-hecke-decomposition-matrix-is-dominance-unitriangular] is not used in the proof and is only recorded for the degenerate comparison. No choice.

items.title: Canonical bases do not solve arbitrary positive-characteristic decomposition numbers
items.statement: The characteristic-zero theorems of this page ([[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]], [[thm-graded-decomposition-numbers-equal-canonical-basis-coefficients-in-characteristic-zero]]) compute graded decomposition numbers of graded Specht modules as global-basis coefficients. In characteristic $p>0$ the factorization [[thm-positive-characteristic-decomposition-polynomials-factor-through-adjustment]] reduces the graded decomposition matrix to a product of the adjustment matrix and the SAME global-basis coefficients, but the adjustment matrix is generally nontrivial: the theorem computes no adjustment entry and asserts no identity adjustment matrix in general. Consequently the characteristic-zero canonical-basis theory does not by itself solve the decomposition-number problem in arbitrary positive characteristic; the general problem retains the boundary recorded in [[rem-general-modular-decomposition-numbers-are-not-determined-by-triangularity]] and [[rem-general-type-a-decomposition-numbers-remain-unsolved]]. This remark records the boundary; it carries no proof obligation and no choice principle.
items.strategy: Compare exactly what the two cited results determine: the characteristic-zero identifications compute $[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]_q$ as $d_{\lambda,\mu}(q)$, while the positive-characteristic factorization leaves the adjustment coefficients $a_{\lambda,\nu}(q)$ undetermined beyond bar-invariance, nonnegativity, unitriangularity and the dominance support of [[def-graded-adjustment-polynomials-in-positive-characteristic]]. The source's announced specialization to James's matrix concerns the degenerate parameter and is outside this page's regime (recorded in the coverage). items.title: Projective and simple Grothendieck classes in a small non-semisimple block
items.statement: Take $F=\mathbb C$, $\xi=-1$ (so $e=2$), level one $\Lambda_0$ and $d=2$. Then $H^\Lambda_2=H_{\mathbb C,-1}(S_2)$ with $T_1^2=-2T_1-1$, i.e. $(T_1+1)^2=0$; the algebra is $\mathbb C[t]/(t^2)$ with $t=T_1+1$, a local algebra whose unique simple is $D=\mathbb C$ with $t$ acting as $0$, and whose regular module is the unique indecomposable projective $P=H^\Lambda_2$. Both partitions of $2$ have content $\alpha_0+\alpha_1$ in the charge-$0$ convention, so $\alpha_0+\alpha_1$ is the only nonzero block and $H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1}=\mathbb C[t]/(t^2)$; its transported grading has $\deg t=2$ (the KLR block is the rank-two $e=2$ block $F[t]/(t^2)$ with $\deg y_2=2$). The graded Specht modules are the one-dimensional modules $S(2)=\mathbb C$ and $S(1,1)=\mathbb C$, both with trivial underlying action of $t$, and the graded composition series of $P$ is $0\subset tP\subset P$ with $tP\cong D\{2\}$, so $$[P]=(1+q^2)[D]\quad\text{in }G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1}),\qquad [P]\notin\{[D],q^{\pm1}[D],\dots\}.$$ The restricted label is $(1,1)$ (since $(1,1)$ is $2$-restricted and $(2)$ is not), the edge degrees of the two shapes are $\deg(S(1,1))=0$ and $\deg(S(2))=1$, so the graded Specht classes are $[S(1,1)]=[D]$ and $[S(2)]=q[D]$, and the level-one Fock data give $G(1,1)=M_{1,1}+qM_{(2)}$ and $G^*(1,1)=(M_{1,1}+qM_{(2)})/(1+q^2)$; hence under the transported identifications of [[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]] $$[P]\longmapsto G(1,1)=M_{1,1}+qM_{(2)}=(1+q^2)G^*(1,1),\qquad [D]\longmapsto G^*(1,1).$$ The graded Cartan pairing of [[def-graded-cartan-pairing-between-projectives-and-modules]] has $h([P],[D])=1$ and $h([P],[P])=1+q^2$, while the graded composition multiplicity is $[P:D]_q=1+q^2$ (ungraded value $2$). Thus the projective class $[P]$ is not a simple class, and the two bases are dual to each other under $h$ without being equal as classes. All computations are finite and explicit; choice is inherited only through the transported identifications cited.
items.strategy: Compute in the algebra: $T_1^2=(\xi-1)T_1+\xi=-2T_1-1$ gives $(T_1+1)^2=0$; the algebra $\mathbb C[t]/(t^2)$ is local with radical $(t)$ and unique simple $D=\mathbb C$, and the regular module is the unique indecomposable projective because a local algebra has a unique simple and its regular module is projective; the graded composition series follows from $tP\cong D\{2\}$ (multiplication by $t$ shifts degree by $2$) and $P\cong D\oplus tP$ as graded vector spaces. The block statement uses the residue-content computation: nodes of $(2)$ have residues $0,1$ and nodes of $(1,1)$ have residues $0,-1\equiv1$, so both lie in the block of content $\alpha_0+\alpha_1=\alpha_1+\alpha_0$; the transported grading is [[cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading]]. The Fock identities are the explicit $e=2$ computation of [[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]] (its recorded $e=2$ example), the graded Specht degrees are read from the degree recursion of [[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]] (the unique tableau of $(2)$ has degree $d_A(2)=1$: the addable $1$-node $(2,1)$ lies strictly below the removable node $(1,2)$, and there is no removable $1$-node below it), and the projective/simple identifications are [[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]]. The pairing values are read from $\operatorname{Hom}^0(P,D)=\mathbb C$ and $\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}(P,P)=1+q^2$ (endomorphisms are the identity and multiplication by $t$, of degree $2$). No choice.

items.title: Specializing the grading variable to one forgets graded decomposition information
items.statement:
Let $q$ be the grading variable and work in the rank-two $e=2$ block of [[ex-projective-versus-simple-grothendieck-classes-in-a-small-block]], where $[P]=(1+q^2)[D]$ and the graded Specht classes are $[S(1,1)]=[D]$, $[S(2)]=q[D]$. Then:

1. the Laurent polynomials $1+q^2$ and $2$ are distinct in $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ but equal at $q=1$; correspondingly the graded classes $[P]=(1+q^2)[D]$ and $2[D]$ are distinct in $G_0^{\rm gr}$, while the forgetful map $\zeta$ of [[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]] sends both to $2[D]$;
2. the graded classes $[S(1,1)]=[D]$ and $[S(2)]=q[D]$ are distinct in $G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1})$, while the forgetful map $\zeta$ of [[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]] sends both to $[D]$; correspondingly the graded transition polynomials $d_{(1,1),(1,1)}(q)=1$ and $d_{(1,1),(2)}(q)=q$ are distinct in $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ but equal at $q=1$. Thus the nonzero off-diagonal graded coefficient $q$ of the standard vector $S_{(2)}$ becomes invisible at $q=1$, where both standard vectors have the same ungraded decomposition data.

So no specialization $q\mapsto1$ determines the graded decomposition multiplicities, the graded Cartan entries or the shift classes; the graded information lives precisely in the $q$-degrees. This is a genuine failure of injectivity of the forgetful map, not a failure of well-definedness. No choice is used.
items.strategy: All statements are read off from the explicit rank-two computation of [[ex-projective-versus-simple-grothendieck-classes-in-a-small-block]] and the defining expansion $S_\mu=\sum_\lambda d_{\lambda,\mu}(q)D_\lambda$ of [[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]] (there $G(1,1)=M_{1,1}+qM_{(2)}$ gives $d_{(1,1),(1,1)}=1$, $d_{(1,1),(2)}=q$, hence $[S(1,1)]=[D]$ and $[S(2)]=q[D]$ are distinct in $G_0^{\rm gr}$ but equal after $q\mapsto1$). The counterexample is a direct finite computation; no choice.
